title: A root set's unit cache is marked used only when an index is built, so prune_indexes can remove one in daily use
goal: _unit_cache_open sets the kbunits*.sqlite mtime only when weighed() runs (an index build); serving from an existing index (_mark_used, kbfacts.py near 2118) never touches it, so a root set used daily on an unchanged kb leaves its unit cache unmarked and another root set's build prunes it after PRUNE_OTHER_ROOTS (14 days), forcing a cold re-weigh (about 11 s on the Windows host; no wrong result); _mark_used also marks the root set's unit cache, or prune_indexes judges a kbunits-rX file by its set's newest kbindex-rX file, and prune_indexes' docstring stays true (found by the SP-yzgetyu2 review)

run: import inspect,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbfacts as k;s=inspect.getsource(k._mark_used);sys.exit(0 if '_unit_cache_name' in s else 1)

repro_reason: the behaviour needs 14 days of file age; the repro reads whether _mark_used marks the unit cache
